text:
Alice (runtime): heads up — saw a sustained p95 token-latency bump on route `chat.generate` since the kernel-selector change. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/runtime/route/chat.generate :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Ben: saw it too. looks correlated with batch-shape shift after the new kernel heuristics went live. not sure if it's batching or kvcache thrash.
Sunita: kvcache miss rate jumped ~3x for long conversations (~>1024 tokens). could be prefix slicing change interacting with continuous batching.
Raj (ml): profiling dump from a sample run:
```
kernel_selector: chosen xformers_fast in 72% of calls, fallback reference_cuda in 28%
avg_batch_size before: 10.4 -> after: 7.1
queue_wait mean: 18ms -> 26ms
per-token exec time tail increased at token 20+
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.89 -> 0.71 for sessions >1024
```
Raj (ml): fallback rate increase is suspicious — fallback kernel has worse per-token throughput so it amplifies tail latency when batcher slices sessions.
Eva (observability): added a temporary panel showing token-level latency breakdown (decode vs kernel vs queue wait) and a batch-size histogram by route. query: `SELECT route, token_pos_bucket, percentile(latency, 95) FROM token_metrics GROUP BY route, token_pos_bucket`
Ben: where is the histogram? can we overlay kernel type? would help prove fallback correlation.
Eva (observability): yep — added kernel_type as series. early look: high p95 coincides with `reference_cuda` spikes. attaching screenshot in #eng-runtime (posted).
Alice (runtime): action items: 1) run replay for top 3 offending traces with `--force-kernel=xformers_fast` vs `--force-kernel=reference_cuda` 2) capture batcher trace with `CONT_BATCHER_TRACE=1` 3) reproduce kvcache behavior with synthetic long prefix workload.
Ben: I'll run replays now, will also flip the continuous-batcher heuristic to prefer larger batches (tune: max_batch_delay_ms from 10 -> 20) to see if mean batch size recovers.
Sunita: I'll generate kvcache microbench with session lengths [256,512,1024,2048] and include random prefix slices to replicate slicing.
ci-bot: replay job 1891234600 started (replay-id=orion-379). logs at https://ci.internal/replays/orion-379
Raj (ml): quick note — if we see fallback due to sequence-length estimation mismatch, we should consider exposing a sampler flag to avoid prematurely switching kernels for borderline seq lengths.
Alice (runtime): agreed. also thinking we should surface a per-route fallback-rate alert (threshold 5% over 5m) and a KV-cache drop alert (delta > 0.05 over 10m). Eva, can you add?
Eva (observability): will add alerts and a pinned dashboard tab for `chat.generate` with: batch_size_hist, queue_wait_p95, kernel_fallback_rate, kvcache_hit_ratio, token_latency_by_pos.
Ben: replay results: forcing xformers_fast reduces p95 token latency by ~38% on the sampled traces. forcing reference_cuda reproduces current elevated tail.
Sunita: kvcache microbench shows hit ratio drop tied to how the prefix is chunked for the cache key — when batcher slices into 512-token subrequests the per-request cache warming is worse.
Raj (ml): that suggests two contributing factors: (1) kernel fallback increases per-token cost, (2) batching-induced cache fragmentation increases misses. compounding effect explains the non-linear tail.
Alice (runtime): plan: revert kernel-selector change for the short term (rollback) while we ship a fix: (a) adjust selector thresholds for seq length, (b) change batcher to prefer slightly larger batches for chat.generate, (c) improve kv cache keying/aggregation for sliced prefixes. I'll open a PR with rollback and tickets.
Ben: +1. will include perf test in release checklist.
Eva (observability): deployed dashboard changes and alerts. will notify if alerts fire.
Alice (runtime): thanks all. we'll reconvene after the rollback and validation run. :thumbsup:
